stories.title: Futures thinking as an everyday design practice
stories.summary: Designers are revisiting the Three Horizons framework to navigate organizational change. The community continues to develop methods for understanding user needs, improving usability, and connecting complex systems. The goal remains to make better decisions about which new features to build, assuming the future is something one can design.

stories.title: Four hidden dimensions of effective teams
stories.summary: A designer argues that team success relies on using context and information with purpose rather than following a magic formula. The author suggests that designers should move beyond viewing their value as purely cosmetic. The reflection follows a design convention held in Lima, Perú.

stories.title: Designing for the AI agent customer
stories.summary: Personal AI assistants are increasingly comparing and purchasing products on behalf of users. Marketing tactics traditionally used to persuade humans are proving ineffective against these automated agents. The shift suggests that current persuasion strategies may soon require an update for a non-human audience.

stories.title: The design process is changing
stories.summary: As the design process becomes increasingly intelligent, practitioners are questioning the nature of their evolving roles. The shift toward automated design workflows raises concerns about whether the industry is asking the right questions as it integrates new technology into its core functions.

stories.title: Beyond the pixel: Reclaiming design as a reflective practice
stories.summary: Reflective thinking is being positioned as a necessary edge for designers in the age of AI. The argument suggests that the focus should shift from faster execution to deep reflection on design action. Speed, it seems, is no longer the primary competitive advantage.

stories.title: Immersive no-code tools reduce cognitive load for novice VR
stories.summary: A study of sixty-three undergraduates found that low-fidelity no-code tools provide a middle ground between 2D interfaces and complex game development software. While traditional 2D software remains superior for basic usability, immersive tools help students conceptualize 3D environments. The software is learning to be less demanding.

stories.title: Human factors engineering shapes next-generation interfaces for AI
stories.summary: Researchers argue that the clinical success of AI in endoscopy depends on interface design as much as algorithmic precision. Poorly structured interfaces risk inducing alarm fatigue and eroding professional trust. The study suggests that technical capacity is only as effective as the human's ability to interpret it.

stories.title: Human factors engineering for AI-assisted endoscopy
stories.summary: A new framework aims to align AI information delivery with the cognitive processes of endoscopists. The authors warn that poorly designed systems can diminish trust and increase cognitive load. The clinical impact of AI is currently tied to how well the interface manages the user's attention.

stories.title: Simulated decision support design reveals intraoperative requirements
stories.summary: Researchers conducted a three-phase qualitative study to address the needs of perfusionists managing cardiopulmonary bypass machines. The role requires rapid adaptation to physiological variables under severe time constraints. The study aims to tailor decision support systems to this safety-critical environment where minor misjudgments carry significant risks.

stories.title: New Orbit ultra-low satellite brand identity
stories.summary: Manual has created a brand identity for New Orbit, a company building ultra-low Earth orbit satellites. The design uses charged-particle dots and crisp schematics to explain the physics of 180 km proximity. The studio says the challenge was helping partners grasp what that distance actually unlocks.

stories.title: Terminal Design Solutions cuts through urban clutter
stories.summary: Founded in 2026, Terminal Design has introduced a collection of machined aluminum street furniture. The benches and lean bars are designed to regulate circulation and occupation in public spaces. The studio aims to provide bold, functional anchors for the public realm through its industrial design practice.

stories.title: TCED Worldwide unveils refreshed brand identity
stories.summary: TCED has updated the branding for its private-label brand, TCED Worldwide. The company states the refresh provides a more distinctive presence in the market for its energy solutions. The brand continues to expand its product offerings to meet the evolving needs of professionals across North America.

stories.title: Inside the graphic design history of the world’s underground networks #ArtTuesday - Adafruit
Inside the craft of Pooch & Mutt packaging design
stories.summary: Robot Food redesigned Pooch & Mutt packaging to move away from a clinical aesthetic. The new look features a soft serif wordmark and line-drawn dogs to emphasize warmth. The studio used a color-coded system to distinguish between various product ranges, aiming to be a partner in pet care.

stories.title: Stockholm Design Lab 1998 to 2025 monograph
stories.summary: The new monograph from Stockholm Design Lab packs 27 years of work into 456 pages. The book jacket continues a visual joke from the studio's first volume, which featured an alkaline battery. This version uses a smaller battery size and a red numeral to mark the passage of time.

stories.title: Daejeon studio No-Name Press turns local identity into design
stories.summary: No-Name Press is a graphic design studio in Daejeon founded by Park Soo-yeon and Jang Young-woong. The studio focuses on embedding regional culture and identity into its graphics. It seeks to explore the boundaries between regions through its design work and local perspective.

stories.title: Korean type designer finds her voice in Berlin
stories.summary: Type designer Hahm Min-ju is gaining attention for her visually striking Hangul typefaces. Her 2018 release, Dunkel Sans, is noted for its maverick quality. The designer is currently based in Berlin, where she continues to treat typefaces as a primary design element rather than just text.

stories.title: A decade of book design with Shakespeare
stories.summary: Yu Jiwon, director of the Geul Culture Research Institute, works across typography, research, and lecturing. After studying in Seoul and Leipzig, she built her career at Minumsa. Her work is grounded in the belief that design roles are interconnected through a shared foundation in typography.

stories.title: Who draws the in-betweens?
stories.summary: Dior released a holiday short directed by Sylvain Chomet, the animator behind The Triplets of Belleville. A week after the release, viewers had paused, zoomed in, and counted the fingers to conclude the work was AI. The internet has reached its verdict on the animation.

stories.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
stories.summary: AI companies are marketing personal agents to handle digital drudgery, but new research suggests they struggle with the details of daily life. According to the ShellBench benchmark, models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Safety requirements were also frequently missed.

stories.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
stories.summary: Walmart is partnering with Meta to let customers shop Black Friday deals through the Muse AI agent. Customers can tell the agent what they want, bypassing Walmart's website. While Amazon has moved to block third-party AI agents from making purchases, Walmart is moving in the opposite direction.

stories.title: New Gemini setting lets you keep chat history, but turn off AI training
stories.summary: Google is rolling out a privacy setting for the Gemini app that allows users to keep their chat history while opting out of generative AI model training. The setting is enabled by default, meaning future chats will not be used for training unless users provide feedback.

stories.title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps
stories.summary: Anthropic is allowing users to install Claude Artifacts as standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows. The feature, currently in beta, lets users keep artifacts in the dock and use OS APIs to create custom terminals or file managers without writing any code.

stories.title: Anthropic gives Claude users a new way to make Mac apps
stories.summary: Anthropic has released a feature allowing Claude users to turn custom tools into personal desktop apps for Mac and Windows. The artifacts get their own icons and windows, requiring user permission before interacting with the computer. Users choose the level of access granted to each app.

stories.title: Anthropic reports 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads
stories.summary: Anthropic reports 700 million monthly downloads for its Model Context Protocol SDK two years after launch. The company is expanding the protocol to allow AI agents to coordinate workflows and communicate with each other. New features include background tasks and follow-up questions for users.

stories.title: Harvey reports legal-task gains for open-weight models
stories.summary: Harvey reports that its Muse Spark Open model reached a 30.3 percent all-pass rate on the Legal Agent Bench after applying its Tenet post-training recipe. The company noted that its model-based grader showed no significant preference improvement for the work products produced by the models.

stories.title: Meta brings Muse AI assistant into Instagram DMs
stories.summary: Meta has integrated its Muse AI agent into Instagram direct messages. The feature allows users to ask the AI for context about posts or products without leaving the app. The move reflects the ongoing competition to embed AI assistants into the everyday digital lives of users.

stories.title: Adobe discounts Creative Cloud Pro for Black Friday
stories.summary: Adobe is offering discounts of up to 77 percent on Creative Cloud Pro plans through November 27. Eligible first-time subscribers can access the individual plan for 29.99 dollars per month, while students and teachers receive a larger reduction. The company's deepest price drops typically occur around Black Friday.

stories.title: Penpot bets on open source design
stories.summary: Penpot presents itself as an open source alternative to Figma and Canva, focusing on cloud collaboration without proprietary licenses. The browser-based tool allows for real-time design and prototyping. The company suggests users review its plugin ecosystem against dominant industry standards before committing to the platform.

stories.title: Canva opens creative platform to AI ecosystem
stories.summary: Canva has made its Model Context Protocol generally available, allowing AI agents and applications to access its design tools. The update includes new REST APIs and expanded command-line support. The company aims to bring visual generation capabilities directly into automated workflows and AI-driven conversations.

stories.title: EMEET PIXY Wireless wins 2026 Good Design Award
stories.summary: The EMEET PIXY Wireless streaming camera has received a 2026 Good Design Award. This marks the second consecutive year a product in the PIXY series has been recognized by the organization. The company continues to highlight its focus on combining intelligent technology with user-centered design.

TheLogoBase launches free in-browser design studio
stories.summary: TheLogoBase has launched a browser-based creative studio for gamers and streamers. The platform includes a logo maker, AI cutout tool, and 3D esports player card generator. It is designed to allow users to customize and download high-resolution graphics without paying freelance fees or recurring subscription costs.

stories.title: Canva expands MCP access for developers
stories.summary: Canva has updated its Model Context Protocol to provide small business owners with new REST APIs and a command-line interface. The update allows businesses to integrate design capabilities directly into their own applications. The company aims to streamline how visual branding is incorporated into third-party products.

stories.title: Willow iOS 2.0
stories.summary: The latest version of the Willow iOS app allows users to dictate text without switching between applications.

stories.title: JSW Motors reveals logo ahead of December launch
stories.summary: JSW Motors has unveiled a new logo for its upcoming passenger vehicle business. The design features a stylized oval emblem with upward-sweeping elements, intended to represent movement and progress. The company plans to debut the badge on its first vehicle when it launches on December 3, 2026.

stories.title: JSW Motors unveils brand identity
stories.summary: JSW Motors has introduced a new logo featuring two ascending forms within a continuous ellipse. The company says the design draws inspiration from India's unity in diversity, symbolizing the relationship between tradition and progress. The badge will appear on all vehicles and across customer touchpoints starting December 3.

stories.title: JSW Motors sets sights on democratizing mobility
stories.summary: JSW Motors has revealed its new logo ahead of its December 3 launch. The company says its ambition is to democratize world-class mobility and bring global technology to India. The badge will feature on every vehicle and across all customer touchpoints, from dealerships to digital platforms.

stories.title: JSW Motors Unveils Its Brand Identity Ahead of December Launch - evo India
JSW Motors reveals brand philosophy
stories.summary: JSW Motors has unveiled its brand identity and logo ahead of its December 3 launch. According to the company, the logo depicts a philosophy where different elements and perspectives find meaning when unified, mirroring the diversity of Bharat. The badge will be used across all customer touchpoints.

stories.title: Jio launches Happy New Year 2.0 plans
stories.summary: Reliance Jio has introduced new prepaid recharge plans offering unlimited 4G and 5G data alongside free Canva subscriptions. The plans include 28-day and 365-day options, with a Nite Data offer available from midnight to 5 AM for users to stream and upload without using daytime data allocations.

stories.title: EPACK Durable expands beyond air conditioners
stories.summary: EPACK Durable is diversifying its product range to include air-fryers and nutriblenders alongside its traditional air conditioner business. Originally established in 2003 as an OEM manufacturer, the company is now seeking to broaden its involvement within the Indian consumer durables market to support long-term growth.

stories.title: NAMI vinyl bar opens with focus on sound
stories.summary: NAMI, a new listening bar in India, features a hi-fi system designed for a vinyl-led music experience. Conceived by Sumit Vaswani, the space draws inspiration from the Japanese word for wave, incorporating concepts like cymatics and waveforms to prioritize sound vibration over simple listening.

stories.title: What Makes a Laminate the Right Choice for Modern Indian Homes? - Realty Plus Magazine
Maple raises $5.3 million for privacy-focused AI
stories.summary: Maple has raised $5.3 million for an AI app designed to keep user data private, even from the company itself. The startup uses open-source code and trusted execution environments to allow users to verify that their information remains encrypted and inaccessible to the developers.

stories.title: Leash Biosciences raises $11 million for AI training
stories.summary: Leash Biosciences has raised $11 million to build experimental environments for scientific AI agents. The startup aims to bypass the slow pace of physical lab work by letting agents replay experiments that have already been conducted, providing the data needed to train AI for scientific discovery.

stories.title: Marlowe raises $277 million for AI inference
stories.summary: Marlowe has raised $277 million to build infrastructure specifically for AI inference workloads. The startup plans to leverage emerging chips and hardware-software co-design to improve compute efficiency and reduce costs. Lior Susan has joined the company as executive chairman to oversee the development of these systems.

stories.title: AidenAI raises $32 million for enterprise workflows
stories.summary: Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 million in a Series A round led by A91 Partners. The company plans to use the capital to expand its platform and engineering talent. Founder Srinivas Kamadi launched the firm in 2023 following a two-decade career at Infosys.

stories.title: Supertake Raises $20M to Turn Market Predictions Into AI-Managed Stock Portfolios - gadget.qoo10.co.id
Iconic raises $10 million for capital project software
stories.summary: Iconic has secured $10 million in seed funding to build AI software for capital projects. The tool connects design, engineering, and contract data to flag flaws and contradictions before they result in rework. The startup has signed five clients since mid-2025 that each spend over $1 billion annually.

stories.title: CortexSpark Ventures launches deeptech fund
stories.summary: CortexSpark Ventures has launched a 1,000 crore rupee fund to back deeptech startups. Founded by former Infosys executives, the firm will invest in areas including spacetech, robotics, and AI. The fund includes an additional greenshoe option of 400 crore rupees for commercializing intellectual property.

stories.title: Stepping back from design work
stories.summary: Stepping back from hands-on design work can feel like losing one's career. The shift requires addressing the psychological transition that occurs when moving beyond a Senior Designer role.

stories.title: Architecture firms list new job openings
stories.summary: Architecture and design firms including Rapt Studio and Cass Calder Smith have posted new job openings in New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Darien. Available roles range from designers with five years of experience to project architects with over twelve years of professional practice.

stories.title: Oprah And Canva Teach Us How To Conduct Layoffs Humanely - Forbes
Kiersten Burton reflects on her final semester at Kennesaw State
stories.summary: Kennesaw State University student Kiersten Burton is preparing to graduate with a degree in Graphic Communications. A student assistant for the university marketing team, Burton is currently reflecting on her academic journey and the personal support systems that shaped her experience before entering the workforce.

stories.title: Neeraj Bhatia appointed director of Columbia urban design program
stories.summary: Architect Neeraj Bhatia has been named the new director of the urban design program at Columbia University. Succeeding Kate Orff, Bhatia plans to introduce a new course focused on ethics, justice, and urban design. He is known for his previous work regarding climate and housing.

stories.title: St. Lawrence College faculty union raises concerns over program cuts
stories.summary: St. Lawrence College is cancelling or suspending several programs, including its User Experience Design course. The faculty union reports that more than a dozen full-time teaching positions are affected, with six roles being eliminated entirely. The college has not provided a timeline for the remaining cuts.

stories.title: Bray Leino Appoints Katy Hopkins as Executive Creative Director , LBB - LBB - Little Black Book
Seven habits for improved listening and trust
stories.summary: Developing better listening habits involves giving people full attention and understanding their perspectives without offering immediate judgment. The practice aims to strengthen relationships and build trust by focusing on what others communicate rather than preparing a response. Listening remains a challenge for those focused on their own speech.

stories.title: Neville Brody joins Toaster as creative chair
stories.summary: Graphic designer Neville Brody has joined the agency Toaster as creative chair. His appointment follows a month of movement across the creative industry, including shifts at TBWA and Uber. Design is reportedly playing a larger role across the sector, even in legal AI firms.

research.title: A simple metal is hiding a strange new form of magnetism
research.summary: Scientists have discovered a strange form of magnetism in an ordinary-looking metal that has no overall magnetization yet profoundly changes how electrons behave. The breakthrough offers a promising new path toward understanding exotic quantum materials and developing future electronic technologies.

research.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Constellations of Colour: Mapping Semantic Neighbourhoods in CLIP
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: How do vision-language models organise the cultural and perceptual dimensions of colour language? This pictorial presents a research-through-design visualisation of colour semantics in CLIP, a pretrained vision-language model. A dataset of 2,500 named colours is embedded. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Construct Validity of AI-Administered Cognitive Assessment: Psychometric Validation of a Nine-Dimension Process-Oriented Evaluation Instrume
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Process-oriented evaluation of large language models requires psychometrically defensible instruments, yet the measurement tools used in AI cognitive assessment have received little formal validation. This paper reports the construct validation of a 54-item, nine-dimension instrument operationalizing. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Cultural and Regional Influences on Global AI Apprehension
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The discussion surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) is primarily influenced by Western viewpoints, often neglecting the cultural, regional, and socio-political factors that affect global perceptions of AI. This study examines how these factors shape AI apprehension in. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Do Simulated Users Push Back Like Real Users? Correctness vs. Stance
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-simulated users stand in for people in multi-turn evaluations, on the assumption that they react to what the assistant says. We test this for pushback. From WildChat, we take conversations in which the assistant explicitly challenges. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Do as I Say, Not as You Do: Assessing Public Versus Practitioner Perspectives on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Language Tec
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: With the public awareness of artificial intelligence (AI) applications such as large language models (LLMs) and generative text-to-video models reaching unprecedented levels, there is an increasing need to reconcile the perspectives held by informed practitioners, who. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Environmental Interaction: Recognizing Capability within Everyday Actions
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Systems designed to support everyday capability consistently ask people to do something additional: track activity, follow programmes. For those who need such support most, this ask is often too high. We propose a different approach: environmental. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
